video.title: The Most Overlooked Side Hustle You Can Start From Home

summary: Chris Koerner visits his neighbour Rayma, a stay-at-home mom of four in Dallas who runs Gifty Gal, a corporate gifting business focused on personalised prospecting gifts for tech sales teams. She started in 2022 with baby shower gifts, grossed about $75k (netting $7,800) in year one, and reached $357k revenue and $119k net in 2025 working about 20 hours a week from home and a shared warehouse. Growth came entirely from referrals and LinkedIn after one LinkedIn post reshared by her husband's network. She explains her pricing (about $100 per prospecting box, 30-50% net margin target, shipping billed separately), wholesale sourcing via Faire and reseller licences, and a four-step framework: connect, collaborate, curate, fulfil.

speakers.name: Rayma
speakers.description: Founder of Gifty Gal (giftygal.co), Dallas corporate gifting business, stay-at-home mom of four

ideas.name: Personalised corporate prospecting gift boxes
ideas.one_liner: Curate and ship personalised, branded gift boxes that sales teams send to prospects and clients to get meetings and responses.
ideas.business_model: Per-gift product sales with a markup on wholesale-sourced items; shipping billed at cost (client's or negotiated rates); minimum order sizes.
ideas.customer: Sales reps and account managers at corporations, mainly tech companies headquartered in Dallas; also internal team and holiday client gifts
ideas.problem: Prospects and decision makers are swamped with generic gifts and cold calls; sales reps' time is expensive and wasted assembling and shipping gifts themselves
ideas.offer: Gifts tailored to each recipient (alma mater, hobbies, kids' schools) with the client's logo, handwritten cards, premium packaging and full logistics

pricing.model: Per box, priced within the client's budget; shipping extra
pricing.notes: Minimum 10 gifts per order and $50 per gift. Target 50% net margin, never below 30%. Shipping is not built into the price; uses client's corporate shipping accounts when available.

acquisition_channels.details: LinkedIn posts; first corporate client came after one LinkedIn post was reshared by her husband's corporate network. LinkedIn is her main lead source; clients posting the gifts on LinkedIn bring new leads.

quote.text: Instagram's not even my platform, it's LinkedIn. That is where [clears throat] I get the most lead generation from
quote.speaker: Rayma

acquisition_channels.details: All clients from referrals and word of mouth; first sales rep client introduced her to other sales reps.

quote.text: they have all been referrals and word of mouth
quote.speaker: Rayma

acquisition_channels.details: Tried Instagram ads; nothing took off.

ideas.delivery: Rayma does proposals from home and fulfils 9am-3pm a couple of days a week in a shared warehouse (grew from 400 to almost 1,500 sq ft). Sources wholesale online (Faire, vendor wholesale programmes), local vendors for customisation, custom boxes from China (20-25 days by sea), in-house laser engraver; packs with crinkle paper; ships via the client's shipping accounts or her negotiated rates.
unit_economics_claims: $100 average prospecting box, goal 50% net margin, minimum 30%
2025 revenue $357k, net $119k, about 20 hours a week
10 gifts x $50 = $500 gross, about $250 net, about 5 hours of work (about $50/hour)
ideas.startup_cost: Under $1,000 claimed; she paid $800 for expedited LLC/EIN; boxes about $5 and bubble wrap about $2 each; can start from home
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Started 2022 with baby shower gifts; first corporate client after a LinkedIn post (timing not stated)

acquisition.how: Driven by personal LinkedIn presence and referrals; content can be drafted by AI but relationships with sales reps are human. Cold email to limited companies is legal in the UK and could be automated.

onboarding.how: Discovery call to learn about each recipient; an intake form could capture recipient details but personalisation judgement is human.

delivery.how: Physical sourcing, engraving, packing and shipping; agents could do product research and shipping labels, but assembly is manual.

billing.how: Quotes and invoices can be automated once the box is defined.

support.how: Order status and tracking questions can be handled by agents; issues with breakages need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Corporate gifting to B2B sales teams works in the UK; would need UK wholesale sources and VAT registration once over threshold; alcohol gifts need care with licensing and recipient preferences. UK GDPR applies to recipient personal data (home addresses, hobbies) collected for personalisation.

risks: Physical, labour-intensive fulfilment limits automation and scale
Thin margins if not buying wholesale (her first year netted about 10%)
Seasonal crunches and expedited shipping costs from overseas suppliers
Single mistake with a corporate client can damage reputation
Handling recipients' personal data for personalisation raises UK GDPR obligations
Lead source concentrated in personal network and referrals

tactics.name: Connect, collaborate, curate, fulfil framework
steps: Connect: post on LinkedIn about what you do (e.g. help sales teams close more deals with personalised gifts) and respond quickly
Collaborate: discovery call with the client on what the gift must achieve and who it must reach
Curate: source products at the best wholesale price that fit the recipient's alma mater, hobbies etc.
Fulfil: assemble, collect shipping info, double-check names and addresses, ship

quote.text: You need to connect with the people, you need to collaborate with them, you need to curate, and you need to fulfill
quote.speaker: Rayma

tactics.name: Wholesale setup to protect margin
steps: Form an LLC and get an EIN
Open a separate business bank account
Get a reseller's licence and wholesale accounts
Buy through Faire or ask brands directly for wholesale programmes
Bring customisation in-house (laser engraver) or use local vendors

quote.text: I knew immediately I need to get a wholesale account and a reseller's license
quote.speaker: Rayma

tactics.name: Bill shipping separately
steps: Quote the gift price without shipping
Use the client's corporate shipping account where possible
Otherwise use negotiated carrier rates (ask FedEx/UPS for a rep, or ShipStation, Pirate Ship, Stamps.com)
Confirm shipping cost after a sample is approved

quote.text: don't make it into your prices or you'll sell yourself short
quote.speaker: Rayma

tactics.name: Minimum order rules
steps: No gifts under $50
No orders under 10 gifts

quote.text: I have minimums now where I don't do gifts um under 50
quote.speaker: Rayma

tactics.name: Launch with one LinkedIn post amplified by a network
steps: Post on LinkedIn announcing the business
Have a spouse/friends in corporate reshare to their networks
Say yes to the first inbound corporate request and learn the domain
Ask that first client to introduce you to other sales reps

quote.text: he reshared my post which went to his whole network
quote.speaker: Rayma

tactics.name: Sell on the rep's cost of time
steps: Calculate how long it takes a rep to source, pack and ship a gift
Compare against the rep's hourly value
Pitch outsourcing as cheaper and faster

quote.text: I did the numbers of how much it takes or how much time it takes me to put a gift together and how much that costs
quote.speaker: Rayma

warnings.warning: Buying products at retail and marking them up for consumers was not profitable; she netted only $7,800 on $75k in year one.

quote.text: I had no clue. I didn't know how to price things
quote.speaker: Rayma

warnings.warning: Trying to serve both B2C and B2B at once caused financial trouble.

quote.text: I made the unfortunate decision to try to market to both B2C and B2B, and that really caused me a lot of troubles financially
quote.speaker: Rayma

warnings.warning: Unplanned expedited shipping from China (normally 20-25 days by sea) ate into profit around deadlines.

quote.text: it also dipped into my profit because I didn't anticipate an expedited shipping cost from China
quote.speaker: Rayma

warnings.warning: Building shipping into your gift price undersells you; bill it separately.
Crinkle paper and packing supplies are surprisingly expensive and sneak up on you.

quote.text: fun fact crinkle paper is actually pretty expensive
quote.speaker: Rayma

warnings.warning: Missing state filing deadlines or EIN filings can get you in trouble.
Be careful with assumptions like alcohol in personalised gifts.

quote.text: Do they drink? Do they not drink? Like, you have to be really careful with something like that as well
quote.speaker: Rayma

lessons.lesson: Generic gifts get ignored because decision makers receive many; personalised gifts researched from sales-call details get responses.

quote.text: these prospects are getting hammered with gifts that are generic all day long
quote.speaker: Rayma

lessons.lesson: A product people naturally photograph and share turns clients into the marketing channel.
Start with low-stakes consumer work to learn, then move to B2B where one mistake can cost the reputation.

quote.text: The stakes are much lower with a baby shower gift
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pick one customer type; focusing on corporate and being strategic with pricing drove the jump to six figures net.
Your real competitor is often the customer doing it themselves; educate them on the cost of their time.
Shared warehouse spaces with flexible leases bridge from home to a full warehouse; a one-year lease helps negotiate price.

quote.text: I do a year lease because that also helps with the price negotiations of the unit
quote.speaker: Rayma

lessons.lesson: Packaging and first impression matter as much as contents.

quote.text: the packaging is just as important as the contents inside
quote.speaker: Rayma

lessons.lesson: Be willing to say no to clients and jobs that do not fit, and set minimums.
Every business is find the customers and fulfil the customers.
